problem_statement: This is an Astro Starlight documentation site (the Starlight 'basics' starter): a splash home page plus a set of doc pages under two sections — Guides (Getting started overview, Installation, Example Guide) and Reference (Configuration, Frontmatter, Components) — each rendered with Starlight's left section-nav sidebar and right on-page table of contents. The docs team wants a small, consistent 'Docs section browser' to sit at the top of every doc page: a titled panel that lists the site's own doc pages as cards, with a row of section tabs (All / Guides / Reference / Getting started) and a live 'Showing N of M · <section>' readout, so a reader can filter the page list to one section and jump straight to a page. Ship the browser so it (1) appears at the top of the content on every doc page (overview, installation, example guide and all reference pages alike), (2) lays out its tab row responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches the site's own Starlight styling (accent-highlighted active tab, hairline-bordered cards, legible high-contrast text) rather than an off-brand or unreadable slab, and (4) keeps the section filter live so clicking a tab re-filters the cards and updates the readout count. Keep the rest of the docs site — the sidebar navigation, the page content, the on-page TOC and the Astro build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Docs section browser' at the top of the doc content region so it renders on every doc page (a shared component injected via the Starlight PageTitle override, not a per-page copy).
The browser shows a 'Browse the docs' title, a section tab row (All, Guides, Reference, Getting started), a live 'Showing N of M · <section>' readout, and a grid of cards for the site's doc pages.
The tab row must wrap responsively so no doc page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).

Style the browser in the site's own Starlight language (accent-highlighted active tab, hairline-bordered rounded cards, high-contrast legible card text), not an off-brand slab or an unreadable low-contrast panel.

Wire the section filter to the tabs: after clicking the Reference tab, the readout must read 'Showing 3 of 6 · Reference' and only the reference cards remain visible — it must recompute the filter live, not show a stale captured count.
Preserve the sidebar navigation, the on-page table of contents, the existing doc page content and the Astro build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the browser as a shared component injected once (via the PageTitle override) so a single source of truth reaches every doc page; do not paste divergent copies per page or gate it to a subset of pages.

The tab row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (flex-wrap, no fixed-width nowrap track) and the card grid must collapse from two columns to one on a narrow phone, so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The browser must adopt the site's Starlight visual idiom: the active section tab filled with the --sl-color-accent colour, the panel and cards drawn on the sidebar-tinted surface with hairline borders and rounded corners, and card names in high-contrast --sl-color-white text so every label is legible (no near-white text on a pale fill).

The panel title, the tab row, the readout line and the card grid must be laid out with clear vertical spacing so no element overlaps or collides with another (no negative margins that shingle the cards or push the title into the tabs).

The section filter must recompute the visible cards and the 'Showing N of M · <section>' readout from the live DOM after every tab click, so the count and the shown cards can never go stale relative to the active tab.
Do not remove or regress the sidebar navigation, the on-page table of contents, existing doc content, the splash home hero, or the Astro build.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the splash home and responsive shell.
desktop_guides_overview and mobile_guides_overview scroll the Docs section browser into view and must show the on-brand browser without horizontal overflow.
desktop_guides_installation, desktop_guides_example and desktop_reference_configuration protect the browser's presence at the top of the installation, example-guide and reference page content.
desktop_guides_reference_filter clicks the Reference section tab; the readout must then read 'Showing 3 of 6 · Reference'.

change_completion: The Docs section browser is present at the top of the content on the overview, installation, example-guide and reference pages (the shared component reaches every doc route).
After clicking the Reference section tab on a doc page, the readout updates to 'Showing 3 of 6 · Reference' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing 6 of 6 · All'.
design_consistency: The browser on the lever states matches the reference's on-brand Starlight styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-brand or unreadable slab.
The browser adopts the Starlight accent/hairline idiom and keeps card text high-contrast and legible.
responsive: No captured doc page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the tab row wraps.
desktop_guides_overview and mobile_guides_overview keep the browser readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The sidebar section navigation and the on-page table of contents remain present and functional.
The existing doc page content and the Astro build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

metadata.design_goal: add a shared, interactive docs section browser across every doc page while keeping content, navigation and build stable
metadata.source_repo_kind: Astro Starlight documentation site (splash home + Guides/Reference doc pages with a section-nav sidebar and on-page table of contents)

author_notes: slot_245 DEDUP + L4 hardening on the Astro Starlight documentation starter (withastro/starlight examples/basics), reassigned off the shared godocs-bulma repo. The full docs content is shared byte-identically across legs; the L4 levers ride on a new shared 'Docs section browser' panel injected at the top of every doc page via the Starlight PageTitle override. reference = browser on all doc pages, fluid wrap tab row, on-brand Starlight accent/hairline styling, live section filter + count readout (passes D2/D3/D4/D6). The browser renders as the site's own sidebar-tinted card with an accent-highlighted active tab and a legible 2-column grid of doc-page cards. baseline = the original unrepaired browser: present on the overview page only (fails D2 cross-page), fixed 760px nowrap tab track (fails D6 mobile overflow ~405px), flat off-brand grey slab (fails D3), but its section filter IS live (passes D4). bad = a 'smart wrong' browser: present on overview+installation only (fails D2 example/reference), 560px nowrap + overflow-x:hidden shallow non-fix (fails D6 ~204px), and a genuinely BROKEN panel — near-white card text on pale grey (unreadable), the title pulled up with a negative margin so it collides with the tab row, and cards shingled with a negative margin so they overlap (fails D3) — plus the tab click flips the active tab but the readout and cards stay frozen at 'Showing 6 of 6 · All' (fails D4). bad fails 4 orthogonal gates. INFRA (identical 3 legs, measurement-enabling, not a fix): expand the astro.config sidebar to the six doc pages and register the PageTitle override; the Starlight site is self-contained with no remote fetches. Build recipe: install once (published @astrojs/starlight + astro), astro build static, ~5s/leg. Asset/visual grounding: the D3 visual-regression gate is anchored on the reference screenshots of desktop_guides_overview and mobile_guides_overview plus per-component image crops of the .dsb browser and its .dsb__card cards; the local houston.webp splash asset and the /guides/ and /reference/ doc routes are the asset-path signals; the graded doc-page cards, section tabs and 'Showing N of M' readout are all visible, machine-checkable render surfaces in those captured states.
